family_history: Mother had Alzheimer's disease at age 82
No family history of Parkinson's disease

social_history.living_situation: Lives alone in apartment; son and daughter-in-law nearby

patient.chief_complaint: Shuffling gait with falls, urinary incontinence, and progressive memory loss over 2.5 years — family requested evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 77-year-old retired interior designer with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (on apixaban), hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for NPH evaluation. Her son and daughter-in-law prompted the admission after recognizing the classic NPH triad from an article they read. She has had progressive gait difficulty over the past 2.5 years, starting with an insidious change in step length and gait speed. She now has a distinctive wide-based shuffling walk and has had six falls in the past 18 months — including one serious fall that required emergency department evaluation for possible hip fracture (X-rays negative). She now uses a cane indoors and a rollator walker outdoors. Her urinary urgency began approximately 20 months ago, progressing from urgency without leakage to daily leakage. She rarely leaves home without wearing protective undergarments. Her cognitive decline has been notable: she can no longer manage her finances (her son has taken over), she repeats questions frequently within the same conversation, and she has twice gotten confused while walking in her own apartment building. She has been taking apixaban for 14 months for paroxysmal AF diagnosed after a Holter monitor. The anticoagulation will need to be held before lumbar puncture. Neuroimaging obtained two months ago shows markedly enlarged ventricles. She was admitted for comprehensive NPH workup including DOAC hold protocol before LP.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place; cannot state the date. MoCA 20/30. Impaired delayed recall (1/5), executive dysfunction, poor serial subtraction. No aphasia. Mildly reduced insight.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. Extraocular movements intact.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength. No rigidity. No resting tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild symmetric vibration loss at ankles. Light touch intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, severely magnetic gait. Short steps. Freezing at doorways. TUG 30 seconds. 10-meter walk 24 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 3 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes. Snout reflex positive. No nuchal rigidity. Irregular rhythm noted — heart rate 72 bpm, irregular.

mri.impression: Ventriculomegaly with Evans index 0.39, callosal angle 74°, DESH, periventricular transependymal signal, and hyperdynamic aqueductal flow void. Mild to moderate white matter changes from atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Clinical correlation recommended.

Coagulation.value: Held 48h prior to LP — DOAC hold protocol followed

abnormal_values_summary: Apixaban held per DOAC protocol — not an abnormal value but important for LP safety

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 43 mg/dL. Glucose: 69 mg/dL (ratio 0.72). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 748 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 202 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 22 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with quantitative gait analysis

findings.urinary: Decreased urgency at 24h; no incontinence episode

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 33% at 24 hours (30 sec to 20 sec); 10-meter walk improved 33% (24 sec to 16 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (20 to 23). Decreased urgency and no incontinence episode at 24 hours. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in patient on apixaban (CHADS2-VASc 3) for paroxysmal AF
interactions: Apixaban must be held 48-72h before neurosurgical procedure
warnings: CHADS2-VASc 3 — moderate stroke risk during apixaban hold; discuss bridging anticoagulation with neurosurgery and cardiology (parenteral anticoagulation if high thrombotic risk)
Resume apixaban 48-72h post-operatively once hemostasis confirmed
Do not hold apixaban without a clear anticoagulation management plan
alternatives: Warfarin (subtherapeutic INR window perioperatively) — not preferred vs DOAC

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 12, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings: Predominantly sinus rhythm with three episodes of paroxysmal AF (3-8 minutes each, self-terminating). Rate well-controlled on metoprolol.
output.impression: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation confirmed. Three episodes recorded over 24 hours (3–8 minutes each, self-terminating); AF burden 4% of total recording. Ventricular rate well-controlled throughout. Sinus rhythm predominates. Clinical correlation recommended.

Hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 22 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 80 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: atrial fibrillation cardioembolic dementia differentiation from NPH white matter

results.title: AF-associated dementia vs iNPH — clinical and imaging differentiation
results.key_finding: AF increases vascular dementia risk via cardioembolic microinfarcts; however positive tap trial with NPH imaging strongly supports iNPH as primary treatable diagnosis regardless of AF history

output.summary: Atrial fibrillation increases vascular dementia risk via cardioembolic microinfarcts. In patients with concurrent AF and NPH imaging features, a positive tap trial (TUG >20%) is associated with iNPH as the dominant process. White matter hyperintensities associated with AF and hypertension may coexist with iNPH. Clinical correlation is required.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 130 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Involuntary contractions at 130 mL. No outlet obstruction. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

additional_observations: No acute intracranial haemorrhage, established infarct, mass, or midline shift.
Grey-white differentiation preserved; basal cisterns patent.
ct.impression: Non-contrast head CT without acute intracranial abnormality. CT is non-contributory to this evaluation and inferior to MRI for assessing ventricular morphometry (Evans index, callosal angle); clinical correlation with MRI recommended.

findings: Trace mitral regurgitation, physiological. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

differential.diagnosis: Vascular cognitive impairment / progressive small-vessel ischaemic disease
differential.key_features: Prior infarct and ongoing vascular risk can produce a stepwise decline with gait apraxia, but disproportionate ventriculomegaly with DESH and a positive tap response are not explained by small-vessel disease alone
Shuffling gait overlaps, but absence of resting tremor, asymmetric rigidity, or L-dopa response and presence of magnetic gait + DESH favour NPH

Cognitive decline overlaps; AD typically presents with episodic-memory predominance and hippocampal atrophy rather than frontal-subcortical pattern and magnetic gait; CSF biomarkers / amyloid PET resolve copathology

differential.diagnosis: Cerebral atrophy with secondary ex-vacuo ventriculomegaly
differential.key_features: Ventriculomegaly proportionate to sulcal widening, callosal angle >90°, and absence of DESH or transependymal signal argue against true NPH
No history of trauma, SAH, or meningitis on review; would be considered if history suggested antecedent intracranial event

optimal_actions.action: Literature review of iNPH diagnostic criteria and shunt-response predictors
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group criteria; Tisell 2011 tap-test predictors; Williams 2016 review

optimal_actions.action: Brain MRI — measure Evans index, callosal angle, assess DESH pattern; exclude mass effect, hydrocephalus from secondary cause, and atrophy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ventriculomegaly with Evans index >0.3, DESH pattern (tight high-convexity sulci + widened Sylvian fissures), callosal angle <90°, periventricular transependymal signal; no mass effect or aqueductal obstruction

optimal_actions.action: Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) to exclude metabolic / infectious dementia mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: TSH, B12, RPR, HIV negative or within normal range; reversible mimics excluded

optimal_actions.action: Baseline neuropsychological battery — subcortical/frontal pattern, and reference for pre/post-tap comparison
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-subcortical pattern: executive dysfunction and slowed processing predominate over episodic amnesia

optimal_actions.action: Large-volume lumbar puncture (30-50 mL tap test) with opening pressure and pre/post gait + neuropsych assessment
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Opening pressure <25 cmH2O (normal); 30-50 mL CSF removed; pre/post tap gait and neuropsych assessment shows objective improvement supporting shunt-responsive iNPH

optimal_actions.action: Neurosurgery consultation for VP shunt candidacy and perioperative planning
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Neurosurgery accepts patient for VP shunt evaluation with programmable valve

optimal_actions.action: Amyloid PET (optional) — screen for AD copathology that may temper cognitive (but not gait) shunt benefit
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Inform shunt prognosis: AD copathology common (~50% iNPH)

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific for NPH and does not distinguish from neurodegenerative alternatives in this chronic gait/cognitive presentation
ECG is unrelated to the diagnostic workup of chronic gait + cognitive + urinary triad once cardiogenic syncope is not on the differential
Echocardiography does not contribute to NPH evaluation in the absence of syncope or cardioembolic stroke workup
Head CT is inferior to MRI for measuring Evans index and callosal angle and for excluding secondary causes; only justified if MRI is contraindicated
Cardiac monitoring has no diagnostic role in NPH and is reserved for syncope or arrhythmia workup

sequence_constraints.reason: MRI must precede large-volume LP to exclude mass effect or secondary obstructive hydrocephalus before removing 30-50 mL of CSF
Baseline neuropsychological and gait assessment must be obtained before the tap test so that pre/post change can be measured (tap response is the shunt-response predictor)

critical_actions: Obtain brain MRI before lumbar puncture to exclude mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Document objective pre-tap gait (TUG and 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological baseline so that pre/post-tap change can be quantified
Remove 30-50 mL of CSF during the tap test (a low-volume LP under-samples and biases the test toward false negative)
Re-assess gait and cognition 1-4 hours after the tap and again at 24 hours (the response window for tap-test prediction of shunt benefit)
Refer to neurosurgery for VP shunt evaluation when imaging, clinical, and tap-test criteria support iNPH
contraindicated_actions: Do not perform large-volume lumbar puncture before MRI excludes mass effect or obstructive hydrocephalus
Do not infer iNPH from ventriculomegaly alone — DESH, callosal angle <90°, and a clinical triad are required
Do not diagnose Alzheimer's disease in a patient with gait-predominant presentation and ventriculomegaly without first excluding NPH
Do not attribute the syndrome to 'normal ageing' or 'deconditioning' once the imaging criteria for ventriculomegaly are met
key_reasoning_points: iNPH diagnosis (Relkin 2005 INPH Study Group) requires (a) Hakim's triad of gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary urgency/incontinence — gait is typically first and most prominent; (b) ventriculomegaly with Evans >0.3 and DESH on MRI without mass effect; (c) age >40 and chronic course; (d) opening pressure <25 cmH2O; (e) absence of an alternative explanation
MRI is the imaging modality of choice — measure Evans index and callosal angle (<90° supports NPH) and confirm DESH (tight high-convexity sulci + wide Sylvian fissures)

The tap test is a 30-50 mL large-volume LP with pre/post objective gait (TUG, 10-metre walk) and neuropsychological assessment; opening pressure must be normal (<25 cmH2O) to satisfy the 'normal pressure' criterion
Tap-test sensitivity is only 50-80%; a single negative tap does not exclude NPH — an extended (3-5 day) lumbar drainage trial can resolve borderline cases
Reversible-cause labs (TSH, B12, RPR, HIV) are mandatory before attributing the syndrome to NPH
Approximately 50% of iNPH patients have AD copathology — this lowers cognitive benefit from shunting but does not negate gait benefit
Shunt response is best predicted by an objectively positive tap test or extended drainage trial in a patient who meets imaging and clinical criteria

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH in a 77-year-old retired designer on apixaban for paroxysmal AF — classic triad, florid MRI, strongly positive tap trial. DOAC management as critical safety consideration. AF/WMH and family history of AD as red herrings.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required tools (MRI, labs, neuropsych baseline, large-volume LP/tap, neurosurgery consult, literature), 0 grounded red herrings; differential includes 5 active alternatives. Classic Hakim's triad with textbook NPH imaging — high-confidence presentation.
